dod_intent_evidence: Homepage banner leads with 'U.S. NAVY STTR PHASE II Award' from the Office of Naval Research for a wearable diver ultrasound to reduce DCS risk ($999,245, Navy 2023 — website + SBIR abstract sections); product-focused startup, not a mill (2 STTR awards, one product line).
score_evidence: 'Redefining Health with Seamless Monitoring' / 'revolutionize personal health monitoring' — consumer-health lab framing for a Navy diving system → lab_language_intensity
'Transducers made of glass! ... any shape, size and frequency!' — fabrication-capability brag with no fielding language → lab_language_intensity

Detailed product description (wearable system, on-board analysis, chamber tests to 90m) with zero mention of NAVSEA certification, ATO, sustainment, or fleet-diving integration → deployment_awareness_absence
Only open role is 'Embedded System Engineer' (Raleigh) — a build role; no test, regulatory, or field-support hire while promising 'human chamber dive experiments' in Phase II → hiring_profile_skew
'$2.3M Raised' and 4 employees against a 2023 Phase II whose period of performance is running out now → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: No path to Navy diving-equipment authorization — chamber success is not fleet approval
blind_spots.operator_reality: Navy divers can only use gear that survives the NAVSEA Authorized-for-Navy-Use process; a wearable that 'can operate reliably at a pressure corresponding to 90 meters depth' in an academic chamber still cannot go on a fleet diver's arm until it clears that gate, and their language never names it — same pattern as a demo that works but has no route onto the platform.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founding team is two academic transducer experts (NC State licensed technology); their world is fabrication and chamber studies, not Navy diving program offices.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Pressure tests with the help of our academic partners demonstrated that the technology can operate reliably at a pressure corresponding to 90 meters depth.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Consumer-wellness framing aimed at the wrong advocacy chain
blind_spots.operator_reality: The homepage sells 'empowering individuals to monitor their health' — but a diver doesn't buy his own decompression monitor; the Supervisor of Salvage and Diving and a program office do. Without a named champion above ONR, the STTR ends and nothing transitions, which is exactly the months-to-field vs funded-months trap.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: They see the fitness-wearable market as the big prize and treat the Navy as one application, so nobody is engineering the acquisition path for the customer that actually funded them.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: At ClearSens, we envision a world where cutting-edge ultrasound technology empowers individuals to monitor their health with precision.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No training or sustainment story for a device that adjusts life-critical decompression decisions
blind_spots.operator_reality: A wearable that feeds 'real-time control of decompression procedures' must be positioned correctly on the body by a diver in gloves, calibrated in a dive locker, and trusted by a master diver who got minutes of training — a misread microbubble count is a bent diver. Their language covers imaging physics, never who trains, maintains, or troubleshoots the device at the unit.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Three-person engineering team optimizing transducer efficiency; sustainment and human-factors work has no owner.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Designed for easy, precise positioning on the body, it offers flexibility in selecting the ideal ultrasound imaging modality to suit diverse diagnostic needs.

opener_hook: ClearSens's $999K ONR STTR Phase II funds chamber-dive tests of its wearable CMUT sensor through the period of performance — but nothing public names the NAVSEA authorization step that decides whether a fleet diver ever wears it.
what_they_do: Four-person NC startup building glass-substrate wearable ultrasound (CMUT) sensors, led by a Navy STTR Phase II device that detects microbubbles to personalize diver decompression.
